strengths: Principled theoretical framework grounded in possibility theory, providing rigorous foundation distinct from heuristic EDL approaches
Remarkable simplicity and computational efficiency—single forward pass with ~10 lines of code, making it highly practical
Comprehensive experimental validation across diverse benchmarks (MNIST, CIFAR-10/100, long-tailed, fine-grained, distribution shift) with multiple metrics
Insightful empirical analyses demonstrating proper epistemic uncertainty behavior (Figure 3) and clear ID/OOD separation (Figure 4), revealing pathological behavior in EDL
Thorough ablation studies confirming necessity of regularization components and empirical verification of key approximation assumption (Appendix C)
weaknesses: Critical approximation (Equation 11) lacks rigorous justification—empirically verified only on CIFAR-100 without formal error bounds or analysis of how approximation quality degrades with model capacity, data dimensionality, or domain
High-capacity assumption never formally defined: unclear which architectures satisfy it, how it scales, or how violations affect the method
Theoretical justification for why relative likelihood captures epistemic uncertainty (vs. aleatoric) is asserted rather than proven; connection to deep learning context not rigorously established
Marginal empirical improvements over F-EDL baseline (often < 2%, with overlapping confidence intervals on CIFAR-10; 1.45 points on CIFAR-100), raising questions about practical significance
Aleatoric uncertainty treatment appears ad-hoc: defined only at end as 1-max α_k/α_0 with no justification, no experiments evaluating it, and unclear relationship to possibilistic framework
Design choices lack principled justification: softplus+1 constraint for α_k>1 is post-hoc fix from proof rather than framework principle; regularizer form (Eq. 16) not compared to alternatives
Narrow baseline comparisons limited primarily to EDL variants; missing comparisons with recent Bayesian, calibration (temperature scaling), and other modern uncertainty quantification methods

Hyperparameter selection under-explored: only λ analyzed with 500× variation across datasets (1e-5 to 5e-3, Table 7) but no principled guidance for new domains; λ = 0 causes failure (Table 6) suggesting brittleness

strengths: Principled theoretical framework connecting possibility theory to epistemic uncertainty quantification, providing rigorous mathematical grounding that EDL lacks
Identifies and fixes fundamental EDL pathology (epistemic uncertainty increasing with more data), demonstrated convincingly in Figure 3
Simple and practical method (~10 lines of code) that maintains theoretical rigor, with closed-form solution via Proposition 1

Comprehensive experimental validation across diverse settings (standard, long-tailed, distribution shift, fine-grained datasets) with multiple complementary metrics (accuracy, confidence AUPR, OOD detection)
Strong results on challenging problems, particularly long-tailed settings (68.81 vs 63.73 on CIFAR-10-LT ρ=0.01) and fine-grained datasets, with clear ID/OOD separation (Figure 4)
Thorough ablation studies (Table 6) and analysis validating design choices, with detailed experimental setup enabling reproducibility
weaknesses: Key approximation (Eq. 11) relies on strong 'high-capacity assumption' that leave-one-out loss is independent of constrained predictions—empirically validated only on CIFAR-100, lacks theoretical error bounds, and may fail for under-parameterized or smaller networks
Quantitative definition of 'sufficient capacity' is imprecise; no analysis of approximation error as function of capacity or behavior in under-parameterized regime

Empirical improvements over recent SOTA (F-EDL) are sometimes modest (CIFAR-10: 92.00 vs 91.19, CIFAR-100: 70.85 vs 69.40), with limited statistical significance testing despite standard deviations reported
Limited scope of approximation validation: Appendix C directly verifies assumption on only one dataset; no testing across different architectures or network sizes to determine when assumption holds
Asymmetry of maxitive pseudo-divergence (Eq. 4) lacks justification for why this particular asymmetry is appropriate or how it compares to alternatives
Method specific to cross-entropy loss; extension to other losses (focal, label smoothing) or tasks (regression) is not discussed, limiting generalizability
No computational cost analysis (wall-clock time); practical guidance limited beyond empirical observation that small λ values work (Table 7); unclear scalability to very large models/transformers

strengths: Novel grounding of uncertainty quantification in possibility theory with principled derivation from first principles, avoiding heuristic objectives used in prior work
Remarkable simplicity achieved despite theoretical rigor: closed-form solutions and ~10-line implementation matching cross-entropy computational cost
Comprehensive experimental validation across diverse benchmarks (CIFAR, long-tail, fine-grained, ImageNet, LLMs) with consistent competitive or superior results
Thorough empirical validation of critical approximations (Appendix D) and well-designed ablation studies demonstrating necessity of components
Clear presentation with effective motivation (Figure 2) and revealing analysis showing DAPPr's epistemic uncertainty properly decreases with data while EDL pathologically increases (Figure 5)
weaknesses: High-capacity assumption (Eq. 11) critical to entire framework but lacks theoretical justification with only dataset-specific empirical validation; no formal error bounds; dismissal of low-capacity regime as unimportant is unsatisfying
Approximations from Eq. (10) to Eq. (12) lack rigorous error characterization; quality only validated through loss constancy, not across prediction simplex
Post-hoc uncertainty definitions (aleatoric: 1-max α_k/α₀, epistemic: K/α₀) disconnect from principled framework derivation; lack formal justification for why these are 'correct' measures
Spurious evidence regularizer (Eq. 16) appears somewhat ad-hoc despite ablations showing necessity; no rigorous justification for specific L2 form or why this formulation enforces claimed principle
Modest empirical improvements over baselines (e.g., Table 1: 92.00% vs 91.19% on CIFAR-10); many gains within error bars; limited statistical significance testing
Hyperparameter tuning claims overstated: λ varies 500× across datasets (Table 7); Figure 4 shows dataset-dependent sensitivity; no principled selection method provided
Limited theoretical comparison with recent Bayesian approaches; incomplete analysis of conflicting label edge case; LLM evaluation restricted to single model and base task
Missing formal convergence analysis for min-max optimization; Danskin's theorem application assumes regularity that may not hold; no discussion of computational properties

strengths: Novel theoretical foundation using possibility theory for uncertainty quantification, well-motivated by the limitation of probability theory's complete mass allocation assumption for epistemic uncertainty under incomplete knowledge

Elegant closed-form solution (Proposition 1) under high-capacity assumption and cross-entropy loss, enabling simple and efficient implementation (~10 lines of code) that matches cross-entropy in computational cost

Exceptionally comprehensive experimental validation across 9 diverse datasets (CIFAR-10/100, CIFAR-10-LT, CUB-200, Stanford Dogs, TinyImageNet, ImageNet, OBQA) with multiple metrics and extensive baselines, showing consistent improvements especially on fine-grained and OOD detection tasks
Strong empirical validation of key assumptions through leave-one-out analysis (Section D), comparison with EDL's instability (Figure 5), and ablation studies demonstrating regularizer specificity
Well-calibrated uncertainty estimates with clear separation of ID and OOD samples (Figure 6), along with reliability diagrams showing superior calibration compared to baselines
Clear presentation with good motivation, transparent experimental setup, detailed hyperparameter documentation, and promised code release supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: The critical approximation in Equation 11 is strong and insufficiently analyzed theoretically. While empirically validated in one setting (Section D), it lacks: (1) theoretical bounds on approximation error, (2) analysis of sensitivity to experimental conditions, (3) investigation of when and how badly it fails when violated (e.g., conflicting labels case is mentioned but not thoroughly investigated)

Fairness concerns in experimental comparisons: different baselines receive different hyperparameter tuning effort (Section C.3), some baseline results are borrowed from other papers, and DAPPr consistently gets 'best results from hyperparameter sweep' while tuning effort for baselines is not equally transparent

Claimed 'minimal tuning' is overstated: despite assertions of low sensitivity, λ varies 50-fold across datasets (Table 7: 1e-5 to 5e-3) and requires both hyperparameter and schedule selection, contradicting ease-of-use claims

Limited theoretical analysis of when the method works: (1) intuition for why possibility theory specifically improves OOD detection is unclear, (2) relationship between model capacity and approximation validity unexplored, (3) softplus(·)+1 parameterization prevents principled uninformative initialization but implications are not thoroughly discussed

Statistical significance not rigorously assessed: standard deviations are reported but no hypothesis tests or confidence intervals provided; some improvements are marginal (e.g., 94.39±0.3 vs 94.01±0.1) making it unclear if differences are meaningful

Missing ablations: no investigation of sensitivity to softplus(·)+1 parameterization choice, no robustness analysis in low-capacity regimes beyond brief dismissal, limited analysis of failure modes or performance degradation when sufficient-capacity assumption is violated
Experimental validation of the approximation (Section D) uses specific setup (3 epochs fine-tuning on CIFAR-100) without exploring sensitivity to these choices, limiting generalizability of findings
Minimal impact statement given emphasis on high-stakes applications (autonomous driving, medical diagnosis); more discussion of failure modes and ethical considerations would be appropriate
